messages:
cass: FYI raising an escalation from AcmeCorp. They switched to our int8 quantized embedding variant to save costs and now their embeddings are the wrong size (used to be 1536, now 768). They say production search quality tanked.

maria: Ugh. Do we have a repro request from them? can they dump one full response? :eyes:

elena: from customer (pasted): 
```
POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "rwd-embedding-3-large-int8",
  "input": ["how to reset password"],
  "batch_size": 8
}
```
Response body: `{ "data": [{ "embedding": [ ... 768 numbers ... ] }], "model": "rwd-embedding-3-large-int8" }`

cass: They included older successful call showing 1536 numbers from `rwd-embedding-3-large` (fp16). So sounds like dimension changed with the quantized variant.

jordan: That shouldn't happen — quantization changes numeric format but not vector dimensionality. Possible explanations: 1) They accidentally hit a different model (eg small vs large) due to model aliasing. 2) A regression in the quantized build that rebuilds a different projection head. 3) Post-processing/batching bug that collapses two halves into one.

tim: Also check batching — if the runtime accidentally concatenates token-level rows when batch_size>1 and then slices, could yield half-length arrays. Do we have logs for that customer's request IDs?

elena: They provided request id: rq_8a7f3c2. Logged at 2026-04-05T14:12:07Z. They used batch_size 8.

cass: repro steps I want us to try quickly:
1) Re-run single input with `rwd-embedding-3-large-int8` batch_size=1, record length.
2) Re-run with `rwd-embedding-3-large` (fp16) to compare.
3) Check model variant metadata: `curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/models/rwd-embedding-3-large-int8` -> inspect `dimension` field and `quantization_profile`.

jordan: I'll grab the logs for rq_8a7f3c2 and check the serving node. If it's a runtime bug, we should be able to reproduce locally by loading the int8 weight set and running the projection. Setting batch_size=1 is a good isolator.

sre-bot: incident created: INC-2026-421. Priority: P2. Assigned: eng-ml/jordan, eng-runtime/tim.

maria: Customer asked if switching to fp16 is a safe workaround. Can we recommend that?

jordan: Short answer: yes, fp16 variant should match dimension. Longer: fp16 avoids the quantization conversion path so it should produce the same shape. Recommend: set `model: rwd-embedding-3-large` explicitly and `precision: fp16` if they need a quick fix, and we rotate int8 once we confirm.

tim: Workaround also: set `batch_size: 1` and `pad_to: 0` (no padding) and return a raw shape check. That will help confirm whether it's batching-related.

cass: Action items for support: 1) Ask customer to run the two small calls we suggested and paste responses (or give us a short-lived API key for repro). 2) If they can't, collect the exact request payload + response (we already have request id). 3) Offer credit while we investigate.

elena: Customer ran our suggested single-call repro and returned: `{ "model": "rwd-embedding-3-large-int8", "embedding": [ ... 1536 numbers ... ] }` when batch_size=1. So int8 returns 1536 when single input. When they send 8 items batch_size=8 they get 768 per item.

jordan: That is huge — points at a batching aggregation bug in the int8 serving path. Likely an index stride miscompute when splitting the flat output buffer into per-request vectors. I'll reproduce with a synthetic batch of 8 locally.

tim: I'll add additional logging on the batch-slice routine and push a debug build to canary nodes. If we confirm, we roll a patch quickly.

maria: I've told customer to use `batch_size: 1` or switch to fp16 for now, offered a credit and asked to hold off on reverting quantization flags. They appreciated the credit offer. :thumbsup:

jordan: Repro steps I'm running now (local):
```
# python snippet
from redwood_runtime import InferenceRuntime
r = InferenceRuntime(model='rwd-embedding-3-large-int8')
inputs = ['a'] * 8
out = r.embed(inputs, batch_size=8)
print(len(out[0]))
```
If I see 768 locally, I'll bisect commit that changed batch-slice for quantized backends.

sre-bot: update INC-2026-421: triage complete, category: embeddings / batching / quantization.

cass: Thanks everyone. Jordan/tim please keep me posted and I will coordinate the customer comms. I'll update the ticket with the customer's single-batch reproducible results.

jordan: confirmed locally — int8 path produced 768 for batch_size 8 on a particular compiled kernel commit. Bisect points to commit `b42f3` in runtime-kernel (quantized buffer view change). I'll open an internal PR with fix and request a hotfix canary deploy to dedicated nodes.

tim: Hotfix patch merged to canary. Eng-runtime will monitor canary for 30m then promote.

elena: Customer notified, will test again after promote.

maria: Follow-up: add a unit test for batch slicing on quantized kernels and add a small e2e test in the regression harness.

cass: Great. Closing loop when incident resolved. :white_check_mark:
